props.title: Should you book a jazz duo or a jazz trio?

rows.text: Upright bass and guitar can cover cocktails and dinner together, or just a single hour on its own. It fits in a corner, so it can play venues that don't have space for a full band.
The drums add a steady beat that helps the music reach a bigger crowd, and the brushes keep them soft enough for dinner.

props.html: “[He] was fantastic, he struck the right note (pardon the pun) with our guests by not only playing beautifully, but also by playing quietly in the background so as not to disturb the conversation of our guests. Everyone loved him and would 100% hire him again. He is a tru pro!”
Hoping to end on the dance floor? Tejas Singh can start as a duo and grow to a quartet. Changes Jazz Trio plays the standards with a modern edge.

rows.text: At a client dinner the conversation comes first, so the duo can keep the music low all the way through.
The duo can stop for remarks and awards and pick back up when they're finished. Learn more about our corporate jazz bands.
The duo can play the hour between the ceremony and dinner, and the ceremony itself if you'd like. Looking for jazz from the processional to the last dance? Check out our wedding jazz band.

The duo can play the standards your residents grew up with, and we can set up a regular weekday afternoon in your common area.
The duo can play through a restaurant’s or a hotel’s Sunday brunch from start to finish.
The duo can play the reception or celebration of life after a service, with the songs your family chooses.

items.a: A jazz trio is three musicians. The traditional combos are piano, bass and drums, or organ, guitar and drums. For private events, ours is usually guitar, upright bass and drums played with brushes. A quartet is the same three with a horn or a voice added. Signet Artists books jazz duos and trios across Denver and the Colorado mountains.

items.q: Can we hire a jazz trio for a wedding?
items.a: Yes. The trio can play a processional and a recessional as easily as standards, and they can keep going through dinner.

items.q: Is a jazz duo enough for a big dinner?
items.a: Yes, in many cases. The music only has to sit behind the conversation at dinner, so two musicians can go a long way. If your guest list is much bigger, or your guests are spread across a large space, we'd suggest the trio.

items.q: Can the same musicians play cocktails and dinner?
items.a: Yes, and that's what most people book.
